synopsis: Every drop of the Pacific is removed and the bare seafloor, its ridges and the Mariana Trench stand exposed under open sky in one locked high-altitude shot.
caption:
The experiment: remove the Pacific Ocean.

One variable changed. The water is gone. The basin, the crust and the atmosphere stay exactly as they are.

What you are left with is the real shape of the planet. The deepest point, Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench, is about 10,900 metres down, deeper than Everest is tall. Mid-ocean ridges become the longest mountain range on Earth, and they were always there.

It cannot happen. There is nowhere to put that much water, and the climate would collapse long before the basin emptied.

This is a simulation, not footage. Which part of the seafloor would you walk first?

shots.prompt:
One continuous 8-second take at 24 fps from a physically fixed orbital or high-aerial mount. Camera position, orientation, focal length, focus, and exposure stay identical for all eight seconds. Frame one clearly contains the named real geography and the single altered variable already at maximum strength. Only its visible physical consequence develops through seconds 1-5 and delivers a decisive payoff during seconds 6-8. Diegetic sound is present at seconds 0-1, thins toward near-silence through seconds 3-5, and surges to its strongest impact during seconds 6-8.

The dry western Pacific basin fills frame one beneath a fixed near-orbital camera, bounded by Japan, the Philippines, New Guinea, eastern Australia, and the curved Mariana island arc. The drained ocean basin is already fully legible: grey-brown abyssal plains lie open to daylight, volcanic seamounts cast long shadows, and the Mariana Trench forms a narrow indigo-black cleft beside its island chain. Raking sunlight reveals sediment terraces and pale salt crusts descending toward Challenger Deep. During seconds 1-3, exposed saturated sediment exhales white vapor ribbons and a tan dust sheet accelerates east across the plain. During seconds 3-5, the dust reaches the trench rim and hangs there while every coastline stays fixed at the same pixel coordinates. During seconds 6-8, a fractured section of the steep trench wall releases into the cleft, throwing a radial dust crown upward as the leading dust sheet pours over the edge. Diegetic audio carries dry wind and granular hiss at seconds 0-1, narrows to sparse pebbles at seconds 3-4 and near-silence at seconds 4-5, then rises into a hollow rockfall roar and a heavy basin-scale impact at seconds 7-8.
